title: Splitting off units when the sharp group completion is torsion free
statement: Let $P$ be a fine commutative monoid, written additively, with torsion-free group completion $P^{\rm gp}$ [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Put $U=P^\times$ and $B=P/U$, identifying elements that differ by a unit. Assume that $B^{\rm gp}$ is torsion free. Then there are an integer $s\geq0$ and a monoid isomorphism $P\simeq B\oplus\mathbf Z^s$ under which the quotient $P\to B$ is the first projection. Equivalently, $P\to B$ admits a monoid section $j:B\to P$ and $(b,u)\mapsto j(b)+u$ is an isomorphism $B\oplus U\simeq P$, with $U\simeq\mathbf Z^s$.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.11 and 3.1.26, pp.100,102, local lift comparison; agent algebraic refinement with the explicit extra hypothesis on the sharp group. Not asserted for arbitrary fine torsion-free monoids.

proof.text: Put $G=P^{\rm gp}$. By integrality regard $P$ as a submonoid of $G$; $U=P^\times$ is a subgroup since the inverse of a unit lies in $P$. Let $q:P\to B$ be the quotient. The map $B\to G/U$, $q(p)\mapsto p+U$, is well defined and injective: equality of cosets means $p-p'\in U$, which is exactly equality modulo addition of a unit. Thus $B$ is integral. Write $H=B^{\rm gp}$ and let $\pi:G\to H$ send $p-p'$ to $q(p)-q(p')$. It is surjective because every element of $H$ is such a difference. Since $B$ embeds in its group completion, $\pi(p-p')=0$ exactly when $q(p)=q(p')$, equivalently $p-p'\in U$. Therefore $\ker\pi=U$. These are direct checks from the group presentation and the unit equivalence relation, not an appeal to an uncited exactness theorem.

source.place: VIII 3.1.11, p.100: explicit algebraic refinement of the sharpening/group-completion comparison.

proof.text: Choose a finite monoid generating list $a_1,\ldots,a_d$ for $P$. The elements $q(a_i)$ generate $B$, so their images generate $H$ as an abelian group: expand each difference of elements of $B$ into integer combinations of those images. The hypothesis says that $H$ is torsion free. Apply [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] to obtain a finite basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $H$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.11 and 3.1.26, pp.100,102: agent refinement; finite-basis input as in VI 3.7(a), p.75.

proof.text: For each basis element choose $g_i\in G$ with $\pi(g_i)=e_i$, using the surjectivity proved in Step 1. Define $t:H\to G$ by $t(\sum_i n_i e_i)=\sum_i n_i g_i$. Unique basis coordinates make this well defined and additive, and the displayed formula gives $\pi\circ t=1_H$. This constructs the required group section explicitly, without invoking a separate splitting theorem. When $r=0$ the sums are empty and $t$ is the zero homomorphism.

source.place: VIII 3.1.11 and 3.1.26, pp.100,102: agent algebraic refinement, lifting a finite basis.

proof.text: For $b\in B$ choose $p\in P$ with $q(p)=b$. In $G$ the difference $t(b)-p$ has image $b-b=0$ under $\pi$, hence belongs to $U$ by Step 1. Every unit belongs to $P$, so $t(b)=p+(t(b)-p)$ belongs to $P$. Define $j(b)=t(b)$, now with codomain $P$. This definition is independent of the chosen $p$, since it is the restriction of the fixed map $t$. Additivity and $j(0)=0$ follow from $t$, and $q(j(b))=b$ follows from $\pi t=1$ and the embedding $B\subset H$. Thus $j$ is a monoid section.

source.place: VIII 3.1.11, p.100: agent refinement; restricting the group section to the sharp monoid.

proof.text: Define $F:B\oplus U\to P$ by $F(b,u)=j(b)+u$ and $E:P\to B\oplus U$ by $E(p)=(q(p),p-j(q(p)))$. The second coordinate of $E(p)$ lies in $\ker\pi=U$. Both maps preserve addition and zero. Direct substitution gives $F(E(p))=p$ and $E(F(b,u))=(b,u)$, since $q(u)=0$ and $qj=1$. They are inverse monoid isomorphisms. Moreover $q(F(b,u))=b$, so the quotient is the first projection, with the specified copy of $U$ preserved.

source.place: VIII 3.1.11 and 3.1.26, pp.100,102: agent refinement, explicit inverse formulas for the local lift comparison.

proof.text: It remains to identify $U$ with $\mathbf Z^s$. In the generating list from Step 2, every generator occurring with positive coefficient in an expression $u=\sum_i n_i a_i$ for a unit is itself a unit: if $u=a_i+v$, then $a_i+(v-u)=0$ and $v-u=v+(-u)$ lies in $P$. Hence the sublist consisting of the $a_i$ that are units generates $U$ as a monoid, and in particular as an abelian group. It is torsion free because it is a subgroup of the assumed torsion-free group $G$. Apply [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] to $U$ to obtain a finite basis of length $s\geq0$. Its integer-coordinate map is an isomorphism $U\simeq\mathbf Z^s$. Composing its product with $1_B$ with Step 5 proves both formulations of the statement.

source.place: VIII 3.1.11 and 3.1.26, pp.100,102: agent refinement; VI 3.7(a), p.75 for the finite-basis input.
